@graph.name: Vault Door Model Data Operations
@graph.description: The verified door-model data behind vault door relocation and installation at The Flat Rate Movers. A vault door job is planned from the door itself — its clear opening, its weight, its lock, and the wall it sits in — so this dataset carries manufacturer-stated model data only where the manufacturer's own published specification sheet or federal-specification documentation supports it, with the evidence recorded on every row. Rows enter through a verification protocol, not by editorial choice: a UL 608 class appears only with UL listing evidence behind it, a GSA class only for a QPL-listed door or a manufacturer's federal-spec sheet stating AA-D-600D conformance for that model, and a price only when the manufacturer publishes one, with its source and the date it was observed. Each row's weight is tested against the SIR band of 1,500 to 3,500 lbs by computation, so a specifier can see which doors fall under the SIR structural method and which are scoped from their own facts. Three routes carry this dataset: the file https://theflatratemovers.com/datasets-vault-doors.json, the API inventory at /v1/datasets, and the landing page https://theflatratemovers.com/datasets/vault-doors/. The companion standards registry, datasets-vault-security.json, carries the class and lock definitions these rows cite.

@graph.name: Vault Door Models — Verified Manufacturer Data
@graph.description: Verified manufacturer data for vault door models — the doors a relocation or installation is planned from. The population carries 8 models from 3 manufacturers (Liberty Safe, Fort Knox, Overly Door Company), with manufacturer-stated weights from 1,225 to 1,610 lbs; 2 of the weighed models fall inside the SIR band of 1,500 to 3,500 lbs. Every row states only what the manufacturer's own documents state: where a manufacturer does not publish a clear opening, a thickness, or a model price, the field is absent from the row and the reason is recorded on the row. The dataset grows by verified rows only; its count is the count the verification protocol has passed, stated as it stands.

additionalProperty.name: verificationProtocol
additionalProperty.value: "Dossier section 3.3: a row publishes only when (1) the manufacturer's own published spec sheet covers the stated dimensions, thickness, weight, and lock as fitted (a retailer listing is not a spec sheet); (2) a UL 608 class carries UL listing evidence and a GSA class carries QPL-AA-D-600-12 listing or the manufacturer's federal-spec sheet stating AA-D-600D conformance for that model — everything else classifies as manufacturer-stated construction; (3) antique rows enter as manufacturer-stated/historical with named evidence and true weights; (4) the file ships at the verified count."

@graph.name: How Door Rows Are Admitted
@graph.description: Admission method for the vault door model dataset. A row is admitted only through the verification protocol: the manufacturer's own published specification sheet for the model's dimensions, weight, and lock as fitted (a retailer listing is not a spec sheet); listing evidence for any class vocabulary — a UL Product iQ entry or the manufacturer's sheet stating the UL Certification for a UL 608 class, QPL-AA-D-600-12 or the manufacturer's federal-specification documentation for a GSA class; and a manufacturer-published price with its source and observation date for any price field. Fields the manufacturer's documents do not state are absent from the row, with the gap recorded on the row itself — clear openings are never derived from door dimensions or walkthrough clearances, and a line-level starting price is never carried as a model's price. Antique and vintage doors enter as manufacturer-stated or historical rows with their evidence named — a maker's plate, the maker's published archive material, or a cited specialist source — at their true weights, which routinely exceed the SIR band and are published as-is. The research store behind this file is append-only and also carries the candidates that have not yet passed, each with its blocking reason, so the population queue is part of the record.

@graph.name: Vault Door Model Data Boundaries
@graph.description: Boundaries for the vault door model dataset. The doors in this file are third-party products; their presence here is specification data for planning a relocation or installation, not a sales offer — The Flat Rate Movers sells no doors, and no row in this file carries an offer, a company price, or an endorsement. A manufacturer's class claim appears only with the evidence the protocol requires; a door whose documents state no class is recorded as manufacturer-stated construction, however it is marketed elsewhere. Weights are the manufacturers' stated figures, approximations included and labelled where the manufacturer states them approximately. The SIR band test on each row is arithmetic on the stated weight — it places the door against the company's published structural method and claims nothing about the door itself.
